p.i: simoniam & corporum puritatem fuit salu-bre, nunc suspectum est remedium, ob id non tentandum: quia huius ætatis corpora plenio revictu multum excrementosa sunt reddita, ob id ad febres putridas opportuniora, in quas diariæ in talibus prompte degenerant, quæ homines sæpe interimut. Ne igitur febre à te excitata hominem perijsse calumnientur propinqui, potius quàm spasmo, à febri excitanda abstine.

Balnea quoque purgato rite toto corpore præsertim naturalia: vt, sulfurea, salsa, alumino-sa, laudantur multum: & quæ à nobis ex sulfure, sale, alumine in aqua coctis fiunt, ac etiam ex decocto herbarum cerebralium, maiorana, salui-a, betonica, chamæmeli, rorismarini, aut ex sanguine bubulo ab animali calē te: dum enim à singulis partibus materiæ reliquias resoluent, nullum erit periculum, ne fusa à balneo in partem distentam confluat.
Suffitum quoque, et vaporem prædicti decocti per lapides ignitos, præcipuè pyrites, aut lateres coctiles in cacabū iniectos excepisse toto

page.notes: Catchword "toto" is set at the right after the last line and is included as a catchword-style word; the marginal reference "Aph.21.5." is a note. Several words are uncertain, e.g. "alumino-sa" and "calē" are read as printed; "excepisse" may read differently. Some letters in the running head and italic text are faint.
